duration_model.expr: offset + (indur2 if ef2 >= 1 and ea2 >= 1 else (indur1 if indur1 < indur2 else indur2))

description: Makes a bridging interpolation between two spectra: a single analysis window is grabbed from each infile (at start/end times in infile1) and the output crossfades frequency and amplitude between those two FROZEN states - unlike morph morph, which interpolates the evolving spectra window by window. Pinned to submode 1 (output level is the direct interpolation result); submodes 2-6 shape the output level from the infile amplitudes (2 moment-to-moment minimum, 3 follows infile1, 4 follows infile2, 5 moves from file1's level to file2's, 6 the reverse) - same argv shape, reachable via execute(). All seven parameters are optional flags. Output duration: offset + indur2 with default ef2/ea2 (verified on equal and unequal input pairs); setting ef2 or ea2 below 1 changes the rule to the SHORTER input's duration (see known_issues). Deterministic (decoded data chunks identical across runs). Both inputs must share analysis parameters ('Incompatible analysis-sample-rate' refusal otherwise).
musical_use: A spectral dissolve between two sonic identities - because each end of the bridge is one frozen window, the result is a smooth, ghostly glide between two STATIC colours rather than a living morph (vibrato and internal motion are lost by design; use morph morph when you want them). Works best between stable-spectrum sounds - held vowels, bowed strings, organ tones, resonant drones. sf2/sa2 vs ef2/ea2 set how much of sound 2's frequency/amplitude is present at the start and end of the interpolation: the defaults (0 to 1) give a complete A-to-B bridge; partial values blend fixed proportions for hybrid, suspended in-between timbres. Decoupling frequency from amplitude interpolation (e.g. frequencies morph early, amplitudes late) gives eerie intermediate stages. start/end confine the interpolation to a segment of infile1's timeline; offset delays sound 2's entry, lengthening the output. Resynthesize (auto-PVOC handles it) and layer the bridge under the two sources to smooth a transition in a mix.

offset.description: Time at which infile2 starts relative to the start of infile1 (runtime-enforced 0 to infile1's duration: -a-0.5 and -a3 on a ~2 s file refused 'out of range (0.000000 to 2.020136)'). Adds directly to the output duration (verified: offset 0.5 -> outdur 2.5223 from 2.0230). Scalar only ('brkpnt_files not permitted', parameter 1).

sf2.description: Fraction of the 2nd sound's FREQUENCIES interpolated at the START (CDP-enforced 0-1, default 0). Scalar only ('brkpnt_files not permitted', parameter 2).

sa2.description: Fraction of the 2nd sound's AMPLITUDES interpolated at the START (CDP-enforced 0-1, default 0). Scalar only (parameter 3).

ef2.description: Fraction of the 2nd sound's FREQUENCIES interpolated at the END (CDP-enforced 0-1, default 1). Setting it below 1 also flips the duration rule to the shorter input (see known_issues). Scalar only (parameter 4).

ea2.description: Fraction of the 2nd sound's AMPLITUDES interpolated at the END (CDP-enforced 0-1, default 1). Same duration-rule effect as ef2. Scalar only (parameter 5).

start.description: Time in infile1 of the START window for the interpolation (runtime-enforced 0 to infile1's duration; -f3 on a ~2 s file refused). Default 0. Scalar only (parameter 6).

end.description: Time in infile1 of the END window for the interpolation (runtime-enforced roughly one window to just past infile1's duration: -g3 on a ~2 s file refused 'out of range (0.005805 to 2.025941)' - both bounds input/analysis-rate-dependent). Default: end of file. Scalar only (parameter 7).

examples.description: Full A-to-B spectral dissolve across the whole of sound 1's timeline.
examples.expected_use: Defaults do the classic bridge: starts as infile1's grabbed window, ends as infile2's. Output duration = infile2's duration.

examples.description: Delayed, partial hybrid: sound 2 enters at 0.5 s and only reaches an 80% blend.
examples.expected_use: Suspended in-between timbre that never fully becomes sound 2; output = offset + the shorter input's duration.

known_issues: Duration rule (all verified via pvoc synth round-trips): with default ef2/ea2 (= 1) the output takes INFILE2's duration regardless of which input is longer (2 s + 1.5 s pairs gave 1.5209 and 2.0230 depending only on argument order); with ef2 or ea2 < 1 it takes the SHORTER input's duration (both orderings gave 1.5209); offset adds directly in both regimes (offset 0.5 + ef2 0.8 on the unequal pair gave 2.0201 vs predicted 2.0209). The curated expression encodes all three cases. BANNER DIVERGENCE: the banner's '...outsound ends at end of first sound' claim for ef2/ea2 < 1 is wrong when infile2 is shorter.

AFTA8 DIVERGENCE (trust the binary): afta8's flag map for bridge (-a start, -b end, -c sf2, -d ef2, -e sa2, -f ea2) matches the OLD CDP7 layout; the r8 banner and binary use -a offset, -b sf2, -c sa2, -d ef2, -e ea2, -f start, -g end. The curated flags follow the binary.
All seven parameters reject breakpoint files ('Cannot read parameter N [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.', N = 1-7) - the bridge itself is the only time-variation on offer.

Both inputs must come from the same analysis setup: a -c2048 .ana against a default one refuses 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: Incompatible analysis-sample-rate in input file ...'. Convert both sources with the same PVOC settings (the engine's auto-PVOC defaults satisfy this).
Time-domain input refused ('Application doesn't work with this type of infile.') - inputs must be .ana (auto-PVOC inserts the conversion).
Deterministic: two runs 1.2 s apart are identical in the .ana data chunk (raw-byte comparison is invalid - RIFF date chunk differs; compare data chunks or resyntheses).
offset/start/end ranges are runtime-enforced against infile1's analysed duration (and 'end' against the analysis window), so refusal bounds vary with the input.
